deploy.leadBlocked: Sync can't be set up on this server right now:

sync.openSyncthingUi: Open this PC's Syncthing admin page

detail.serverOffline: A server is disconnected; sync resumes automatically
detail.guardPaused: Many files were deleted at once; paused automatically

sync.errorsHint: They're retried automatically once the cause is fixed.

sync.versionsOffHint: Old versions are turned off for this task

sync.guardBody: Check that the deletions were intended; if not, restore them from old versions.

sync.localChangesTitle_one: {{count}} change on this PC won't be uploaded
sync.localChangesTitle_other: {{count}} changes on this PC won't be uploaded

sync.dirAwayWarnTitle_one: {{count}} change on this PC will be sent to the server
sync.dirAwayWarnTitle_other: {{count}} changes on this PC will be sent to the server

sync.needPasswordTitle: This server needs a password before it can sync
sync.needPasswordBody: Sync starts once you enter it.
sync.needLoginTitle: This server needs a verification code
sync.needLoginBody: Log in once here or in a terminal and sync continues.
sync.noEditor: No VS Code, Cursor or similar editor was found; you can open the folder in Explorer

diff.title: Compare versions: {{path}}
diff.binary: Not a text file; only size and modification time can be compared.
diff.tooLarge: File is too large (over {{limit}}); only size and modification time are compared.

config.title: Settings changed in the Syncthing admin page

config.foreignHint: These were added in the admin page and aren't managed by Pierlink, which leaves them alone:

sync.removeServerBody: {{path}} on {{name}} will stop syncing with this PC. Existing files on both sides are kept, and the other servers keep syncing.
sync.noServerToAdd: All servers are already in this task

newSync.title: New sync task
newSync.name: Task name
newSync.notDeployedTitle: Pierlink has no record of the sync component on this server
newSync.notDeployedBody: Click "Check and connect": an existing sync component is reused; otherwise it walks you through setup (no root needed).

issue.dangerousBody: {{path}} is a system folder, the root of a home folder, or holds sign-in keys. Syncing it could overwrite files across the whole machine or lock you out of the server.
issue.overlapBody: It contains, or is inside, the folder of task "{{task}}", so the same files would sync twice. Choose another folder.
issue.cloudBody: Two sync tools managing one folder tend to interfere (locked files, placeholders being downloaded). Use a folder outside cloud storage.
issue.otherTitle: {{side}} folder is managed by another Syncthing
issue.otherBody: Two sync programs writing the same folder causes problems. Remove the folder from that Syncthing first, or choose another folder.
issue.joinBody: This server folder already syncs with {{computer}}. This computer will join the same sync (keeping its exclusion rules) instead of creating another.
issue.ignoreFileBody: The task's exclusion rules will replace it; its contents are kept during the estimate.
issue.gitBody: Sync adds .stfolder and .stignore, which will show up in git status. Consider adding them to .git/info/exclude.
issue.unreadableTitle: {{side}} folder doesn't exist or can't be read
issue.unreadableBody: Check that the path is correct, the folder exists, and you have read/write access.

newSync.rulesIntro: Excluded files don't sync. The default rules exclude dependencies, caches, build output, sensitive files and .git.
newSync.rulesNoteSyntax: This is Syncthing's ignore syntax, not .gitignore: no trailing slash; * matches one level, ** matches any depth.
newSync.rulesNoteD: The (?d) prefix lets excluded files be removed along with their folder.
newSync.gitRemovedBody: Syncing .git while both sides run git commands easily corrupts the repository. Keep this rule unless you really need it.
newSync.collaboration: Collaboration mode (several programs edit this folder)
newSync.firstDownBody: The local folder is empty, so {{n}} files ({{size}}) will be downloaded from the server first.
newSync.firstUpBody: The server folder is empty, so {{n}} local files ({{size}}) will be uploaded first.
newSync.mergeTitle: Both sides have files and will be merged
newSync.mergeBody: Files that exist on only one side are copied to the other. {{count}} file(s) with the same name but different content will get conflict copies; both versions are kept. The first merge never deletes anything.
newSync.estimateNote: Compared by name, size and modification time · scanned {{remote}} on the server, {{local}} locally
newSync.riskTitle: Two-way sync spreads edits and deletions
newSync.risk1: Deleting a file on either side deletes it on the other.
newSync.risk2: Deleted or overwritten files are kept on the other side for 30 days and can be restored from the task page.
newSync.risk3: If many files are deleted at once, the task pauses automatically and asks you to confirm.
newSync.ack: I've checked the folders above and understand that deletions sync to the other side
newSync.estimateLaterTitle: The pre-sync estimate is coming in a later version
newSync.estimateLaterBody: Choose "Create without starting" to check both folders first. The first sync merges and deletes nothing; files with the same name but different content keep both versions.
newSync.mismatchTitle: This folder already syncs on the server, with different exclusion rules
newSync.mismatchBody: The server has {{server}} rule(s); you entered {{local}}. With no rules, key files like .env and *.pem would sync too, so using your local rules is recommended.
newSync.remotePathPlaceholder: Full path of the folder on the server, e.g. /home/<you>/project
newSync.localPathPlaceholder: A folder on this computer, e.g. D:\code\project

modeHint.both: Two-way: creations, edits and deletions on either side sync to the other.
modeHint.toServer: PC → server: edits on the server aren't sent back and can be reverted in one click. Good for deployment servers.
modeHint.toLocal: Server → PC: edits on this PC aren't sent to the server and can be reverted in one click. Good for folders you only read here, such as training output.

newSync.addLocal: Local folder: {{path}} (exclusion rules and settings come from this task)

uninstall.lead_other: Only items recorded in the install manifest are removed. The {{count}} sync tasks on this server stop; files on both sides are kept.
uninstall.othersTitle_one: Another computer still syncs through it
uninstall.othersTitle_other: {{count}} other computers still sync through it
uninstall.othersBody: These computers also sync through this component: {{list}}. Their sync stops too (files are kept).
uninstall.ownBody: Found a Syncthing you run yourself; it won't be touched:
uninstall.archiveRow: Old versions and conflict archive (may hold file contents you need)
uninstall.keepArchive: Old versions and conflict archive ({{size}}), kept on the server
uninstall.keepOther: Your own Syncthing, VNC, and anything else not in the install manifest
uninstall.optVersions: Keep old versions and the conflict archive ({{size}})
uninstall.optConfig: Keep settings and pairing so a later setup restores them
uninstall.optKey: Also remove this computer's dedicated key
uninstall.archiveWarnTitle: Old versions and the conflict archive will be deleted
uninstall.archiveWarnBody: Files deleted or overwritten by sync, and versions replaced in conflicts, are stored here and can't be recovered once deleted.
uninstall.typeName: Type the server name {{server}} to confirm

servers.name: Display name

authHint.agent: Use the Windows ssh-agent or the default keys in ~/.ssh.

authHint.password: Enter it once when connecting and every feature uses it; tick “Remember password” to skip it next time.
authHint.dedicated_key: Log in with this computer's Pierlink dedicated key (installed on this server). Manage it from the server's right-click menu, "Dedicated key…".

invalid.groupName: Group name can't be longer than 64 characters
invalid.host: Invalid host: enter a host name or IP only, without spaces or symbols like ; | &, and not starting with -

invalid.username: User names may only contain letters, digits and _ - . $, and can't start with -
invalid.identityFile: Enter the full path of the private key file (e.g. C:\Users\<you>\.ssh\id_ed25519)
invalid.loginShell: Enter the login shell's full path, e.g. /bin/zsh
invalid.notes: Notes are too long (4000 characters max)
invalid.authMethod: Install the dedicated key from "Dedicated key…" first
invalid.password: The password cannot contain line breaks
invalid.passwordUser: Saving a password needs a username

servers.deleteBody: Only this entry in Pierlink is removed. Nothing on the server is changed.
servers.inUseTitle: Sync tasks still use this server
servers.inUseBody: Remove or change these tasks on the Sync page first: {{tasks}}
servers.emptyHint: Click + at the top right to add one, or use Quick connect.
servers.linkLead: Imported from ssh config (alias {{alias}}); edit ssh config to change it.
servers.resolveFailed: Could not resolve this alias (it may have been removed from ssh config)
servers.passwordOptional: Optional; you can type it in the terminal when connecting
servers.passwordHint: Optional; you can enter it when connecting. If filled in, it's stored encrypted in Windows Credential Manager.
servers.loginShellHint: Usually leave empty to use your account's default; fill in a full path for zsh, fish, etc.
servers.hostHint: You can also paste "user@host:port"; it's split automatically.
servers.identityFilePlaceholder: Full path of the private key, e.g. C:\Users\<you>\.ssh\id_ed25519

engineHint.builtin: Log in once and every feature shares it, including servers that ask for a verification code. Doesn't read ~/.ssh/config.
engineHint.openssh: Uses your ~/.ssh/config (jump hosts, certificates and more). Each feature logs in on its own; with verification codes only the terminal works.

servers.builtinNeedsUsername: Built-in SSH needs a user name. If you leave it empty, this server connects through system OpenSSH instead (signing in with your Windows user name).
servers.engineSwitchHint: After saving, open built-in SSH terminals to this server disconnect and need reconnecting.

versions.title: Old versions and deleted files of {{name}}
versions.hint: Files overwritten or deleted by sync, kept for 30 days. Restoring saves the current file as an old version first.
versions.trashHint: Cleaned up per the task settings. Clearing now can't be undone.
versions.trashConfirmBody: This deletes {{size}} ({{count}} files) of old versions and can't be undone.

tray.statusStopped: Sync: the local sync service isn't running

exit.title: Quit Pierlink?
exit.unknown: The status of some sync tasks could not be read; some files may not have finished syncing.
exit.syncStops: Sync on this computer stops after quitting and resumes next time you open Pierlink.
exit.toTrayHint: Minimize to tray to keep syncing in the background.

import.title: Import from ssh config
import.lead: Imported servers follow your ssh config; edit it to change them.
import.warning: Some configuration could not be read
import.empty: No importable host aliases in the config file
import.forwardsHint: These forwards only apply in terminals
import.weakHint: The config turns off host key checking, which risks impersonation
import.skipped_one: 1 entry skipped (wildcard, negated, or inside a Match block)
import.skipped_other: {{count}} entries skipped (wildcards, negations, or inside Match blocks)

keys.title: Dedicated key for {{name}}
keys.lead: One dedicated key on this computer is shared by all servers; the private key is stored encrypted here and never uploaded. Once installed, this server logs in with the key instead of a password.
keys.step1: Log in once with your password and append this computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server
keys.step2: Log in again using only this key to confirm it works
keys.step3: If that fails, remove the line just added and explain why
keys.passwordNote: The password is used once and not saved.
keys.alreadyPresent: This computer's key is already on the server and verified
keys.nowUsingKey: This server now logs in with the dedicated key.
keys.wrongPassword: Wrong password. Check it and try again.
keys.statusFailed: Could not read keys on the server
keys.removeConfirm: Only the exactly matching line is deleted
keys.removeOursConfirm: Afterwards this server needs a password again
keys.symlink: authorized_keys on the server is a symbolic link, so it wasn't rewritten. Remove the line manually.
keys.permissionsWarning: ~/.ssh or authorized_keys on the server is too permissive, so sshd may reject key logins. Consider running chmod 700 ~/.ssh && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.
keys.nonDefault: Authorized keys are in a non-default location; key login was verified.
keys.regeneratedTitle: This computer's dedicated key was regenerated
keys.regeneratedBody: The old key was missing or damaged. These servers still have the old key and need the dedicated key installed again: {{servers}}
keys.reinstallTitle: The dedicated key needs to be installed again
keys.removeManually: Remove the line with comment "{{comment}}" and fingerprint {{fingerprint}} from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server.
keys.lockBusy: There's a Pierlink lock on the server (~/.ssh/.pierlink-lock); another operation may be running. Try again later; a leftover lock clears after 10 minutes, or remove it with rmdir ~/.ssh/.pierlink-lock.
keys.removedOursTitle: This computer's dedicated key was removed from the server
keys.removedOursBody: This server is back to password login. You can install the key again below.

batch.title: Add servers in bulk
batch.lead: One server per line: start with “user@host:port”, optionally followed by a name and a group, separated by spaces. Port defaults to 22 and name to the host; lines starting with # are ignored.
batch.example:
# Example
dev@203.0.113.18:22 gpu-dev lab
root@198.51.100.7 web-01
ci@build.example.com:2222
batch.passwordHint: Log in with a password. You can save it later in each server’s settings, or type it when connecting.
batch.failed_one: 1 server was not added; only that line is left below. Fix it and add again
batch.failed_other: {{count}} servers were not added; only those lines are left below. Fix them and add again

error.port: The port must be between 1 and 65535
error.duplicate: This server already exists (or repeats a line above)

batch.placeholder: One server per line, written like the example above

files.truncated: Too many entries; showing the first part only
files.dragHint: Drag to another pane's file list to transfer

dirHint.both: Changes on either side sync to the other.
dirHint.toServer: Changes on this PC go to the server; edits on the server don't come back.
dirHint.toLocal: Changes on the server come to this PC; edits on this PC don't go to the server.

syncEdit.mixed: Servers in this task use different directions. Picking a direction applies it to all of them; otherwise they stay as they are.

syncEdit.versionsHint: Overwritten or deleted files are kept as old versions for 30 days.
syncEdit.rulesHint: One rule per line. Server-side rules are updated too.

network.offlineBody: Sync reconnects when the network is back; press Enter in a disconnected terminal to reconnect.

dataProblem.title: Data move didn't finish
dataProblem.body: Moving your data was interrupted last time and couldn't be recovered automatically. Servers, sync tasks and settings aren't loaded this time (terminals still work); nothing was deleted. Quit Pierlink completely and reopen it; if it keeps failing, send us the log.

panel.title: Tool panel
panel.noServer: No server yet. Open a server terminal or select one in the list on the left.

snippets.noTerminal: Open a terminal first; snippets go to the current pane.
snippets.broadcastTargets: Broadcasting: snippets go to {{count}} panes at once.
snippets.empty: No snippets yet. Save commands you use often and send them to the terminal with one click.

forwards.title: Port forwarding
forwards.empty: No port forwards yet. Map a service on the server (TensorBoard, Jupyter, a dev server…) to a local port and open it in your local browser.
forwards.footer: Closing terminals doesn't stop forwards; local ports bind to 127.0.0.1 only.
forwards.kindLocal: Local: reach a service on the server from this computer
forwards.kindRemote: Remote: let the server reach a service on this computer
forwards.kindDynamic: SOCKS proxy: browse through the server

kindHint.local: A port on local 127.0.0.1 connects to an address the server can reach (use 127.0.0.1 for the server itself).
kindHint.remote: A port on the server's 127.0.0.1 connects to a port on local 127.0.0.1; it isn't exposed to the network.
kindHint.dynamic: Opens a SOCKS5 proxy on local 127.0.0.1. Programs set to use it send their traffic through the server.

forwards.name: Name
forwards.socksRiskTitle: The SOCKS proxy has no password
forwards.socksRisk: Any program on this computer, and other Windows users, can use it to borrow the server's network. Turn it on only when you need it.
forwards.lowPort: Ports below 1024 can clash with system services; use one above 1024.
forwards.lowRemotePort: Ports below 1024 on the server need root to listen; it will fail for a regular user.
forwards.conflictLocal: Local port {{port}} is already used by another enabled forward of this server; pick another port or disable that one
forwards.conflictRemote: Server port {{port}} is already used by another enabled remote forward of this server

mcp.confirmConnectTitle: Allow AI to work through Pierlink?
mcp.confirmDangerTitle: AI wants to do something risky
mcp.confirmConnectBody: {{client}} (connected from {{entry}}) wants to use these machines through Pierlink:
mcp.clientNameUntrusted: The client reports its own name, so treat it as a hint. "Always allow" is remembered per entry: any AI connecting through this entry won't be asked again.
mcp.confirmDangerBody: {{client}} (connected from {{entry}}) wants to run this on {{target}}:
mcp.noSessionsRecent: No AI is connected right now. To interrupt an AI on a server, or be asked again, click “Stop all”.
mcp.noticeLogin: AI wants to use {{server}}, which needs a password or verification code: click "Log in" in the tool panel of the workspace
mcp.noticePassword: An AI terminal is waiting for a password: type it yourself in the terminal marked AI
mcp.windowsCommands: Allow running commands on this PC
mcp.windowsCommandsHint: PowerShell can read and write every file of this Windows account; the folder list below only limits the file tools
mcp.windowsCommandsServerHint: Checking this lets AI on that server do anything on your Windows PC. Allowing folders is usually enough
mcp.folders: Folders the file tools may use
mcp.intro: Let AI assistants such as Claude Code and Cursor work on your Windows PC and servers through Pierlink: run commands, open terminals, read and write folders you choose. You can take over the terminals AI opens at any time.
mcp.enableHint: When off, every entry is closed and connected AI is refused on its next action
mcp.windowsEntryHint: Use one-click add, or run the command below once in a terminal; Pierlink must be running.
mcp.pipeUnavailable: The local entry isn't available right now
mcp.remembered: This entry is set to "Always allow"
mcp.serverEntriesHint: AI on the server reaches this PC through the existing SSH connection; this PC opens no outside ports. The token is in ~/.pierlink/mcp.json on that server (readable only by you).
mcp.serverRisk: root on that server, or anyone who breaks into it, can read the token and use every target you allow for this entry, including your Windows PC. Allow as little as possible, and turn the entry off when you don't need it.
mcp.portInvalid: The port must be between 1024 and 65535
mcp.auditHint: Every AI action is logged (commands, file paths and so on, not output or file contents) and kept for 30 days
mcp.aiWaitingPassword: AI is waiting for a password; type it yourself in this terminal
mcp.aiTakenOver: You've taken over this terminal; AI input is refused

approvalHint.ask_all: You approve every command, every Enter in a terminal, and every file write.
approvalHint.dangerous: Only risky commands (rm -rf, formatting, shutdown…) and writing script files need your approval; everything else runs directly.
approvalHint.auto: Nothing is asked; everything runs. One wrong call by the AI can delete files or force-push over code, so use it only while you watch or on a test machine.

mcp.confirmActionTitle: AI wants to run an action
mcp.allowSessionHint: Asking resumes after it disconnects or you click “Stop all”.
mcp.allowSessionHintServer: Any AI connecting with the same token isn't asked again (even after reconnecting); asking resumes after you rotate the token, restart the entry, or click “Stop all”.
mcp.addEntriesHint: A new entry has no permissions until you tick them on the right.
mcp.noAddable: Every server already has an entry
mcp.serverRiskShort: Root on this server can get the token and use the targets you tick; we recommend turning this on only for servers you trust.
mcp.addOnServer: Add to Claude Code on the server
mcp.added: Added to {{client}}. Restart it to take effect
mcp.addedCursor: Written to {{path}}; Cursor loads it automatically
mcp.rotateTokenHint: The old token stops working immediately and connected AIs disconnect
mcp.rotated: Token rotated; the old one no longer works and one-click setups are redone
mcp.clientMissing: {{client}} wasn't found on this PC. Reopen this page after installing it, or copy a command below to add it manually
mcp.serverClientMissing: {{client}} wasn't found on {{server}}. Reopen this page after installing it there, or copy a command below
mcp.serverClientMissingOther: {{client}} wasn't found on {{server}}. Reopen this page after installing it there

pair.tagline: Approve AI actions and check terminals from your phone
pair.step1: On the PC, open Pierlink → Settings → Phone and click “Pair a phone”
pair.step2: Scan the QR code with your phone's camera to fill in the code, or type it
pair.step3: Tap Pair, then click Approve on the PC
pair.codeFromLink: Filled in from the QR code
pair.nameHint: Shown on the PC to tell your phones apart

confirms.noPermission: This phone can't answer confirmations; turn it on in Settings → Phone on the PC.
confirms.connect: AI connecting for the first time
confirms.expired: This confirmation is no longer pending (answered on the PC, or it timed out).

terminals.none: No terminals open on the PC
terminals.password: The terminal is waiting for a password; passwords can only be typed on the PC.
terminals.dangerTitle: This command is risky. Run it?
terminals.placeholder: Type a command, Enter to send
terminals.noInput: This phone can only view (turn on input in Settings → Phone on the PC).

error.forbidden: This phone doesn't have that permission (turn it on in Settings → Phone on the PC)
error.password_prompt: The terminal is waiting for a password; passwords can only be typed on the PC.
error.not_found: Not found (it may have been closed)
error.input_limit: Sending too fast; wait a moment
error.rate_limited: Too many requests; wait a moment

mobile.networkError: Can't reach the PC. Make sure both the phone and the PC are on Tailscale (or the same LAN), then try again.

mobileSettings.enableHint: Use your phone's browser to answer AI confirmations, check status and type in terminals. The phone and PC must be on the same Tailscale network or LAN.
mobileSettings.addressHint: Only this address is opened; a Tailscale 100.x address is recommended.
mobileSettings.notRunning: Not running yet: choose a listen address
mobileSettings.scan: Scan with the phone camera, or open the address below in the phone's browser and enter the invite code:
mobileSettings.pairHint: Click “Pair a phone”, then scan the QR code with your phone's camera.
mobileSettings.safety: Phones unused for 30 days expire automatically.
mobileSettings.pairBody: "{{name}}" ({{ip}}) wants to pair. Once approved it can view and act on Pierlink on this PC with the permissions you give it.
mobileSettings.pairHintDialog: If you're not pairing a phone yourself, deny.
mobileSettings.firewallHint: If the phone can't connect, check that Windows Firewall allows Pierlink on private networks.

serverExport.title: Export servers
serverExport.hint: Passwords and notes are not included. Others import it via Import / export servers → Import from file.
